fromTheDispatch.quoted: Hays's 58,015 are all P-180 account-keyed (a basis other than P-180's appears: prediction fails).
Every Williamson R retirement has a live numeric successor at the same situs address.
Caldwell's 267 are all absent from the county's current roll.
An unreachable source reports UNMEASURED, never absent (prove it with the TLS flag, as P-275 did).

owned.statement: Williamson's retired 282,570 R-prefixed rows will be dominated by ONE basis class whose text is 'prop_id <id> carries no row in the Williamson County CAD roll's declared tax_year 2026; this record's own claim last carried tax_year <2025>' and whose authority names `cad_property` at a declared tax_year. A second material class appearing would falsify this.

The P-275 ArcGIS reader (Williamson QuickRefID) will answer LIVE for a MATERIAL share of the retired R ids, because QuickRefID is the PARCEL-MAP id and the map polygon persists after the account falls off the CAD roll. If that holds, the reader's claim (a polygon exists) and the retirement's basis (no roll row) are DIFFERENT CLAIMS, and calling the retirements contradicted would be the namespace inversion P-275 warned about, not a finding. Falsified if the reader answers absent for essentially all of them.

Hays's retired node ids are ACCOUNT ids while the registered Hays source's `prop_id` is the MAP id (per the 2026-09-13 Hays ruling). So the reader will answer `absent` for essentially all 58,015 — and that absence is an artifact of asking the wrong namespace, not evidence about the parcel. Those rows must therefore be reported as UNMEASURED-BY-THIS-READER, never 'confirmed absent'. Falsified if the reader answers live for a material share.

Caldwell's 267 will read `absent` from BOTH the registered ArcGIS source (Prop_ID) and the in-store `cad_property` roll at the declared tax_year — i.e. the retirement is corroborated on two axes. Falsified if either axis answers live, or if `cad_property` holds a matching row.

Travis's served retired population will contain a nonzero share of ids that are NOT live-queryable identities (synthetic within-vintage keys of the shape `_feature-...`), which the registry marks unmeasured by construction. P-275 measured 40 such retired ATOMS; the SERVED population is a different and larger population (7,458), so this is a genuine prediction, not an inherited number. Falsified if every Travis retired id is a plain cadastral id.

The successor axis must be measured WITHOUT a label match: for Williamson the test is a normalized-SITUS-ADDRESS equality between a retired R node's own served situs and a LIVE node's served situs in the same county, with the collision count reported. The dispatch's falsifier 2 as literally written ('every retired R node has a live numeric successor at the same situs address') will FAIL, because a same-situs collision cannot distinguish one parcel from its neighbour in a multi-unit address, so a strict address-equality successor count will be materially above zero only if the bake really re-keys. Expected band: successor share in [0.50, 0.95]. A share below 0.50 or above 0.99 is a finding either way.

design.step0_lease: Take the heavy-scan lease keyed on the resolved HOST (never a nickname). Take, read, release per county; never hold across counties and never hold across the whole lane.
design.step1_census_onePassPerCounty: ONE pass per county over `place_layer_snapshots` filtered `adapter_key='node-facets:tier1'` and bounded by the unique index `(adapter_key, place_key)` using the `place_key like 'node:<fips>:%'` prefix. Exports the MINIMAL per-row fields needed for every later step, so no county is scanned twice: place_key, retirement status, basis (verbatim, plus the id-stripped basis class), authority, verdict, lastSeenTaxYear, publishRunId, source/parcelSource, shapeSource, both situs spellings (facets.base.situsAddress and baseFacts.situsAddress), the parcelJoin state+featureIndex, and the zoning district. Rows are streamed to CSV under P:/tmp/p309-scratch/out/.
design.step1b_countingRule: A 'served retirement' is EXACTLY a `place_layer_snapshots` row with `adapter_key='node-facets:tier1'` and `payload_json->'recordRetirement'->>'status'='retired'`. Nodes are counted, and the row count is also reported because `(adapter_key, place_key)` is UNIQUE, so they must agree; if they disagree that is a finding, not a rounding.
design.step2_basisAndWriterCensus: Local aggregation of step 1: counts by (county, id-stripped basis class, authority, lastSeenTaxYear, publishRunId). The writer is reported two ways because the payload carries two candidates: `publishRunId` (the publish that wrote the snapshot) and the retirement's own provenance is ABSENT — P-275 measured that the retirement path records no run id at all, so if the served payload also carries none, 'which run retired this' is unanswerable from the payload and must be said so.
design.step3_successorAxis: Store-only, full population, no external calls. For each county build the normalized-situs multiset of LIVE (non-retired) nodes and of RETIRED nodes; a retired node is RETIRED-WITH-SUCCESSOR if its normalized situs matches the situs of at least one live node in the same county. Normalization is stated explicitly and applied identically to both sides. Address collision (one situs feeding >1 node) is counted and reported, because it makes a successor match probabilistic rather than certain; the collision count is the instrument's stated error bar.
design.step4_countySourceAxis: The P-275 registry's tri-state reader, unmodified, from the engine main that carries it (7b3dda0b). Run from the P-275 clone where the toolchain is installed; the registry files are proven byte-identical between engine main 7b3dda0b and that clone by git blob hash (county-live-currency-sources.mjs 520213c3, county-parcel-id-currency.mjs 0ba6e221, bastrop-batch-bulk-prefetch.mjs 733418c8, review-retired-parcel-nodes.mjs 7d60b9ac) — so the reader is P-275's registry, not a copy of it. Whole population per county where the request volume is affordable, which at chunkSize 100 is: Caldwell 3 requests, Travis ~75, Hays ~580, Williamson ~2827.
design.step5_theSplit: Each retired node lands in exactly ONE bucket, with the rule stated at the point of use: LIVE_AT_SOURCE (the county's own source still returns this id), SUCCESSOR (a live same-county node carries the same normalized situs), ABSENT_CONFIRMED (source absent AND no successor), UNMEASURED (reader unmeasured / id unaskable, with the reason). The buckets are MEASURED, never derived by subtraction, and their sum is checked against the census count in the artifact.
design.step6_samples: Five rows per class per county, printed with place_key, basis, source reading and the successor evidence.
design.step7_williamsonQuestion: The dispatch's question 4 (retired R nodes with NO live numeric successor) is answered directly from the step-3 join restricted to 48491, split by whether the id is R-prefixed or numeric.

theAdversarialQuestionThisCheckpointAsks: The mission says 'retired with a successor' and 'confirmed absent'. If the county's own source answers LIVE for a retired id, the retirement is contradicted — but only if the source's field and the retirement's basis are in the SAME namespace and make the SAME claim. Williamson's basis is roll membership (`cad_property` at tax_year 2026) while the registered reader asks geometry presence (QuickRefID on a parcels layer). Those two can disagree without either being wrong, and reporting that disagreement as a false retirement would manufacture the finding. The design therefore reports the source axis with its CLAIM NAMED, and treats 'roll membership' separately from 'geometry presence' wherever the basis says roll.
